reviews.body:
Thank you. The fix is the right shape, but this PR breaks an e2e test, and the failure is consistent.

**Evidence.** `e2e (1/3)` failed twice on this PR (the first run and a rerun). Both times it was `test/frameworks.integration.test.ts > Reticle connects in each React framework > Astro + React (page script)`, with "@reticlehq/example-astro dev server never served :5304 (last status: no response)". The PR is based on `5f6d3b14f`, and on that same commit the test passes on main in about 4 s. So the change causes it.

**Likely cause (please confirm).** `replacesOurs` is `registered.get(key) !== source`. If discovery builds a NEW `source` value on each pass (a wrapper object or a bound function, not the store instance itself), the comparison is always true. Then every discovery pass calls `registerStore` again. If registering, or the subscription it adds, starts another discovery, the loop never ends. The Astro example renders the React island on the dev server, so a spin there matches a dev server that never answers.

**Fix.** Compare the underlying store instance, not the descriptor that discovery returns. And keep a steady state that does no writes. A test for that: run discovery twice over the same unchanged store, and assert `registerStore` is called once. Then run `pnpm test:e2e` (or at least the integration suite) locally before you push.

You are right, and I was wrong. I called the e2e failure consistent and caused by this change. It was `Node.js v22.23.3 is not supported by Astro!` at `astro dev` startup, which is runner Node drift and nothing in your code. The same Astro test also failed on my own hover PR (#2143) in one run and passed in another, on the same commit. Thank you for checking the log, which I should have read before I guessed at a cause. You also confirmed the identity point: `source` is the store itself, and the new test shows that repeat passes over an unchanged store do no writes. Approved.

comments.body: Thanks for your first pull request to Reticle! A maintainer aims to review within two days. Before then, `pnpm verify` locally catches most of what CI will, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reticlehq/reticle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the rest. If CI does not start, a maintainer needs to approve it for first-time contributors; that is normal.

Thanks. Two things.

1. The comparison is already on the underlying object, not the descriptor: `discoverStores` returns `source` as the Redux store / QueryClient itself, and `registered` maps name -> that source. I added the steady-state test you described (a QueryClient, whose adapter store is rebuilt on every pass, discovered three times: first pass registers, the next two return nothing).
2. The `e2e (1/3)` log shows `Node.js v22.23.3 is not supported by Astro!` printed by `astro dev` before it ever loaded our code, so the dev server exited at startup rather than spinning. Later runs on main and other branches passed, so this looks like runner Node drift; I'd suggest re-running that job.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
